0.content:
Ameyalco Waters (also: Ameyalco): Ameyalco Waters is a coastal stretch of Natlan's Toyac Springs, in the land of the People of the Springs. It is a body of water formed where springs meet the coast, slightly warmer than the surrounding coastal waters, a warmth the official description attributes to magma chambers beneath. It is a place of surfing, Koholasaur riding and the Spiritway.

Status as of 7.1: Open and unchanged as of 7.1; no appearance in 6.x or 7.0-7.1 story content was found.

1.content: Ancestral Temple (also: Temple of Ancient Forebears): The Ancestral Temple is a sacred site on Coatepec Mountain in Natlan where people once communicated with the Night Kingdom. Today the tribes have a steadier link to the Night Kingdom, so the temple is unused, but it is still holy ground, guarded by the Scions of the Canopy.

2.content:
Ancient Mountain Path (also: Flowfire Experimentation Site): The Ancient Mountain Path is an old route on the volcano slopes of Atocpan in Natlan. It holds the Flowfire Experimentation Site, an ancient research station where dragon scholars worked out how to turn liquid Phlogiston into stone while the war against the powers of the heavens loomed. The station was abandoned long ago and is kept only by stone constructs.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the site is still abandoned and open to exploration.

key: Dragons' Residence in the Ancient Sacred Mountain
3.content:
Ancient Sacred Mountain (also: Sacred City of Tollan, Sacred City, Tollan, Land of Primal Flame, Dragons' Residence in the Ancient Sacred Mountain): The Ancient Sacred Mountain is the huge hollow inside the Great Volcano of Tollan in southwestern Natlan. It holds the Sacred City of Tollan, the capital of Natlantea, the dragon civilisation that ruled Natlan before human tribes. Its creator and master, the Pyro Dragon Sovereign Xiuhcoatl, was killed there when the human hero Xbalanque stormed the city, and Xbalanque died with him before being reborn as the first Pyro Archon. The city was then sealed for millennia and overrun by the Abyss. In 5.5 the Traveler, Paimon and the young saurian Little One leapt into the crater, restarted the city's machinery and reached its Heart. There Little One refused to activate Huitzilopochtli, a dragon device that would have burned all Natlan into phlogiston.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Sacred City is an open but ruined area. It has been unsealed, much of the Abyss has been cleared, and Huitzilopochtli was not activated. Kukulkan faded away at the Heart, and Little One, freed of the Flamelord's Blessing, is a small Tepetlisaurus again.

4.content:
Ancient Watchtower: The Ancient Watchtower is a domain in Natlan's Coatepec Mountain area, a ruin of enormous structures built long ago by the dragons of the land. Legend says those colossal beasts, having explored all the land and sea, raised these towers to look out toward the wider world beyond the sky. The dragons are long gone, and nobody today knows the true purpose of the place.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the domain is permanently accessible in Natlan. It carries no named plot; the dragons that built it are described as long vanished.

5.content:
Ashflow Street (also: The Unfinished Ashen City): Ashflow Street is a dead settlement at the foot of the Cradle of Fleeting Dreams in the ruined island of Ochkanatlan, Natlan. The in-game viewpoint calls it the Unfinished Ashen City: a place where people tried to found a new country on the ruins of a city built by a forgotten race, and where only ash remains. The alliance that gathered to build it has long since scattered.

Status as of 7.1: Abandoned and lifeless as of 7.1.

6.content:
Atocpan: Atocpan is the volcanic southwest of Natlan. The Great Volcano of Tollan fills the region, an active volcano that erupts from time to time, and beside it lies the home of the Collective of Plenty (Teteocan), the tribe known for bodybuilding, wrestling and the best fruit and vegetables in Natlan. Ruins of the ancient dragons lie scattered around the slopes. The name Atocpan means "thick and fertile soil" in Nahuatl, which suits the rich volcanic farmland.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Atocpan is quiet, with its tribe prospering and the volcano still erupting now and then.

7.content:
Basin of Unnumbered Flames: The Basin of Unnumbered Flames is the great bowl of land at the centre of Natlan. It holds the Stadium of the Sacred Flame, the nation's core landmark where the eternal Sacred Flame burns and the six tribes gather for the Pilgrimage, along with the fairgrounds and inns that serve it and the smoking Huitztli Hill to the north. Official text says the basin is not natural: something huge once crashed here, and no one knows what.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the basin is at peace. The Stadium hosts the Pilgrimage as a sports competition.

8.content:
Blazing Ruins: The Blazing Ruins are the remnants of a ring-shaped ceremonial site on Coatepec Mountain in Natlan, from an era before people truly mastered flame. Sages from all corners of the world came to ponder fire and tried to perfect the rituals needed to transform phlogiston. Today it is a domain overrun by scoundrels.

Status as of 7.1: Permanently available in Natlan as of 7.1; no plot events are tied to it.

9.content:
Bounama's Grocery: Bounama's Grocery is a small general-goods shop in the Chuwen Fair of the Stadium of the Sacred Flame, in Natlan's Basin of Unnumbered Flames. It is run by Bounama, who is affiliated with the Masters of the Night-Wind, and it sells ordinary cooking ingredients. The shop is open at all hours and restocks every day.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the shop is unchanged since its introduction in 5.0, and no later story role is recorded.

10.content:
Brewblossom Stores: The Brewblossom Stores are an underground facility on Tete Isle, in the Easybreeze Holiday Resort off Natlan's western edge, where Aphimead is refined and stored. Visitors can take part in a hands-on brewing experience called Honeydew Craftbrew.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the facility is open as part of the resort. No role in 6.x (Nod-Krai) or 7.0-7.1 (Snezhnaya) story content is recorded.

11.content:
Castle Joquiratto: Castle Joquiratto is the stronghold of the villain "El Capoctus Joquiratto", the main antagonist of the immersive adventure experience at Villa Guiztli. It sits in the western zone of the Guiztli Ridge caverns in the Easybreeze Holiday Resort. It is a comic, theatrical place full of scheming Nochtli lackeys, capybara and alpaca townsfolk, and booby-trapped chests.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the castle remains part of the resort and has no recorded role in later story content.

12.content:
Catastrophe's Edge: Catastrophe's Edge is an instanced trial area in Natlan's Tequemecan Valley. It lies beyond the Hall of Parting Vows and is entered through a portal during the world quest Revelations from the Past.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the instance remains accessible from the Hall of Parting Vows. No later developments were found.

13.content:
Chamber of Deliberation: The Chamber of Deliberation is the assembly hall in the Sacred City of Tollan, inside Natlan's Ancient Sacred Mountain, where the Thirteen Sovereign Lords of the ancient dragon civilization once gathered to settle administrative and judicial matters. It is now a gold-trimmed, self-repairing ruin, and its preserved council records show a ruling class arguing over how to deal with humanity.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Chamber is unchanged since 5.5: a ruined hall with its records open to the Traveler. No later story use is recorded.

14.content:
Chamber of Night's Trial (also: Trial Grounds of Restive Nightsouls): The Chamber of Night's Trial is a hidden arena in Natlan, in the Night Kingdom, resembling the Stadium of the Sacred Flame. It is entered by a visitor holding a Night Jade. A Nightsoul Spirit there invites the visitor to quiet the restless Nightsouls through battle.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the chamber is still accessible as a permanent hidden challenge; no 6.x or 7.0-7.1 source found mentions it.

15.content:
Chamber of Weaving: The Chamber of Weaving is a minor point of interest within the Masters of the Night-Wind's Sacrificial Altar of Enigmatic Land, in Natlan's Tezcatepetonco Range. Its only listed occupant is the NPC Yolotli, who is affiliated with the Masters of the Night-Wind. Canon says very little about the place itself.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 no change to the Chamber of Weaving is recorded, and it has no known role in later story content.

16.content:
Citlali's Home: Citlali's Home is the residence of Citlali, the great shaman of the Masters of the Night-Wind, in the Tezcatepetonco Range. It stands far from the tribal settlement and is hard to miss: its outer walls are covered in graffiti. Inside it is a mess of wine bottles, snacks and shelves crammed with light novels.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Citlali's Home is unchanged: a permanent instanced interior, with no later story role recorded.

17.content:
Coatepec Mountain: Coatepec Mountain is a towering peak in Natlan and the home of the Scions of the Canopy (Huitztlan), the tribe of explorers, couriers and hunters who live alongside the leaf-tongued Yumkasaurs. Their village hangs from the cliff-face, and the mountain is also the seat of the Turnfire rites in memory of the ancestor Yupanqui. The Pyro Archon Mavuika comes from this tribe. The name means "at the snake hill" in Nahuatl.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the tribe is at peace and Kongamato's corruption is stabilised.

18.content:
Colorfall Cave: Colorfall Cave lies just south of Colorfall Cliffs on the Easybreeze resort island. A crooked sideline used it as a hidden workshop for making fake Koholasaur dolls, and a young painter's apprentice named Zhaka was held there against his will until the Traveler freed him.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the workshop is abandoned and the cave is open.

19.content:
Colorfall Cliffs (also: Airborne Asha): Colorfall Cliffs are the sunny, colour-streaked fields of the Easybreeze Holiday Resort. Above them hangs the resort's star attraction, the Airborne Asha, a floating structure shaped like an Asha holding a torch, which visitors ride a hot air balloon up to and paint.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Colorfall Cliffs are open as a resort attraction.

20.content:
Concealed Land of Enigmas (also: Hidden Land of Enigmas, Enigmatic Land): The Concealed Land of Enigmas is a small cave hidden behind a waterfall west of Wavey Bay, in the Easybreeze Holiday Resort (also called Tenochtzitoc) on Natlan's western edge. A woven-scroll mystic arts implement at its end opens a portal to a temple that the wiki calls the Pyro Archon Temple. It is part of the quest The Last Survivor of Tenochtzitoc, added in 5.8.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the cave and portal are open to visitors; the Pyro Archon Temple can be reached again at will. No new development in 6.x or 7.0-7.1.

21.content:
Core of Chu'ulel (also: Core of Chuulel, Chu'ulel Light Core, Bloodline's Control Hub, New Core of Chu'ulel): The Core of Chu'ulel is a cavern beneath the Vision Serpent's Sanctum in Ochkanatlan, the ruined dragon city of Natlan. Inside is the Chu'ulel Light Core, a glowing orb that pulses like a heart and once powered all of Ochkanatlan. Och-Kan built this core by enslaving his own draconic half, and sealed his mind inside it to fight alongside his people. By 7.1 it has been cleansed of Abyssal energy but is spent, leaving only a piece of Pyrophosphorite.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Core is cleansed but dead: the Light Core lost its last vitality, and what remains is a piece of Pyrophosphorite. Cocouik later regained Och-Kan's body and spoke as him before dying.

22.content:
Cradle of Fleeting Dreams (also: Cradle of Dreams): The Cradle of Fleeting Dreams is the castle-like structure at the centre of Ochkanatlan, the ruined ancient city of Natlan. It stands over Ashflow Street, the settlement at its base, and has a throne at the top of a staircase.

Status as of 7.1: Ruined and abandoned; open for exploration in Ochkanatlan as of 7.1.

23.content:
Derelict Masonry Dock: The Derelict Masonry Dock is an abandoned dragon-era facility hidden deep in the heart of the mountain at Atocpan, in the Remnants of Tetenanco area of Natlan. In its day, ash-gray mechanisms (Secret Source Automatons) driven by golden runes did the labour of flesh there, bringing grand designs to life above pools of flame. It is now a desolate shell.

Status as of 7.1: Permanently accessible in Natlan as of 7.1; no plot is tied to it.

24.content:
Easybreeze Holiday Resort (also: Tenochtzitoc): Easybreeze Holiday Resort is a bright, sparsely inhabited island off the westernmost edge of Natlan. It is also called Tenochtzitoc, the old settlement where the war with the Abyss began and finally ended. The resort opened in 5.8 for a trial summer season: sandy beaches, a market, dance stages and playful Asha, colour-loving mascots that are secretly the souls of people lost in the Mare Jivari. Behind the fun lies the grave of the hero Tenoch and a temple built to hold back the Bakunawa.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the resort is open. Venti and Mavuika have guided the souls who wished to return home out of the Mare Jivari.

25.content:
Easybreeze Market: Easybreeze Market is the commercial heart of the Easybreeze Holiday Resort and often the first place tourists see. It has restaurants, specialty shops and playful decor made by the resort's Asha.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the market is open.

26.content:
Esoteric Arrays: The Esoteric Arrays are a subarea of the Ancient Sacred Mountain, within the Great Volcano of Tollan in Natlan, where the ancient dragons once ran arrays that performed arithmetic calculations. Today the ruins are overgrown with Abyssal corrosion.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Arrays are cleared of corrosion and idle; no later story role is recorded.

27.content:
Fallingstar Fields (also: Tephric Ruins): Fallingstar Fields is a subarea of Atocpan in Natlan. It holds the Tephric Ruins, a section of old ruins that the volcano threw out about five hundred years ago, around the time of the cataclysm. Inside are broken pieces of Secret Source machinery arranged as if for worship, and a hidden room with a sealed report about the dragonborn.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the ruins stand quiet and open; the sealed report can be read.

28.content:
Firethief's Secret Isle: Firethief's Secret Isle is a small island south of Coatepec Mountain in Natlan. It is hidden on the map and under constant cloud until all four of its time-trial challenges are completed. It was an ancient trial site and training ground, and only Saurians live there now.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the isle is a quiet training ground with only Saurian residents.

29.content:
Flame-Melding Ritual Grounds: The Flame-Melding Ritual Grounds are a subarea of the Ancient Sacred Mountain, in Natlan's Great Volcano of Tollan. According to the World Quest Sealed Site of Sacrifice it is where Xiuhcoatl created the first Astral Assemblage, a feat comparable to forging a star. The altar was sealed, and the Traveler unseals it.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the grounds are unsealed and unchanged; no later story use is recorded.

30.content:
Furnace of Fiery Embers (also: Furnaces of Fiery Embers): The Furnace of Fiery Embers names five Source Mechanism sites in Ochkanatlan, Natlan: three in underground caverns (west, southwest and north) and two on small islands (east and southeast).

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the five furnaces remain sites to be rekindled by players. No later changes were found.

31.content:
Golden Dusk: Golden Dusk is a restaurant and lodge in the People of the Springs' settlement at Toyac Springs in Natlan, owned by Kupo Nui, the matriarch of the Nui family. It serves chilled drinks, has beautiful scenery and a convenient beach location, and has an in-house singer, Tirda.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Golden Dusk remains open and steady, with no recorded story role after 5.0.

32.content:
Grand Wrestling Grounds (also: Resonating Arena): The Grand Wrestling Grounds is an elevated arena decorated with massive bull horns in Atocpan, Natlan. It is the central hub of the Collective of Plenty tribe, where its many athletic competitions are held, and is also called the Resonating Arena.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 it is an active arena in Atocpan. No later changes were found.

33.content: Great Volcano of Tollan (also: Volcano of Tollan, Sacred Mountain, Tollan Volcano): The Great Volcano of Tollan is the enormous active volcano that covers Atocpan in the southwest of Natlan. Ancient scrolls call it the Sacred Mountain. It still erupts from time to time and is said to have been far more active in darker ages. It was once the dwelling of the ancient dragons, and the legends of Natlan keep returning to it.

34.content:
Guiztli Path: Guiztli Path is a winding cavern linking Villa Guiztli to Castle Joquiratto on the Easybreeze resort island. It is a stretch of the resort's immersive adventure in which visitors play heroes defending a town from the villain El Capoctus Joquiratto.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the path remains open as part of the attraction.

35.content:
Guiztli Ridge: Guiztli Ridge is a small island of the Easybreeze Holiday Resort, topped by a single rocky ridge. Beneath it lies Villa Guiztli, an underground town that offers a role-play adventure against a make-believe villain.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the ridge remains open as part of the resort.

36.content: Hall of Parting Vows (also: Sacred Path Trial Ruins): The Hall of Parting Vows is an underground ruin in Tequemecan Valley, Natlan, said to be where Xbalanque, the first Pyro Archon, and the Sage of the Stolen Flame swore a sacred oath. Players enter it during the world quest Revelations from the Past, seeking the token the Sage left.

37.content:
Heart of Force Inversion: The Heart of Force Inversion is a subarea of the Ancient Sacred Mountain, in Natlan's Great Volcano of Tollan, filled with pools of liquid phlogiston that flow upwards into the sky. Abyssal corrosion clogs its waterfalls until the Traveler clears it.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the area has been cleansed and is unchanged; no later story use is recorded.

key: True Heart of the Sacred Mountain
38.content:
Heart of the Sacred Mountain (also: True Heart of the Sacred Mountain, Sacred Mountain's Heart): The Heart of the Sacred Mountain is the innermost chamber of the Great Volcano of Tollan, far below the ruined Sacred City in Natlan. It holds the heart of the primal flame (Phlogiston) and the last legacy of the ancient dragons: Huitzilopochtli, the Natlan Phlogistonization Array, a device made to burn Natlan into pure phlogiston and so destroy the Abyss. In 5.5 the Traveler and the saurian Little One reached it, and Little One chose not to run the machine. As of 7.1 it lies dormant and obsolete.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Heart is dormant. Huitzilopochtli has not been activated and is obsolete; Little One keeps a dimmed mark and has returned to his small saurian size.

39.content:
Huha Hill: Huha Hill is the resort's lodging district: a cluster of villas and other places to stay, with rooftop pools, outdoor dining and a fine view of Colorfall Cliffs, Guiztli Ridge and Wavey Bay. A loading screen calls it a great area for tourists and says its name comes from the 'hooh... hah...' sounds often heard nearby.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Huha Hill is open as the resort's lodging area.

40.content:
Huitztli Hill (also: Smoke Ridge): Huitztli Hill is a mountain north of the Stadium of the Sacred Flame in the Basin of Unnumbered Flames. Local tribespeople call it Smoke Ridge because magma streams from the Great Volcano of Tollan run beneath it and send smoke up through its valleys. It is too hot even for people used to Phlogiston, which may be why a reclusive Qucusaur lives there.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the hill is still smoking wilderness.

41.content:
Isle of Tozoz (also: Isle of Night, The Isle of Night): The Isle of Tozoz, also called the Isle of Night, is a small island in the northeastern corner of Ochkanatlan in Natlan. It was once guarded by people who watched over saurian hatchlings and is now a quiet ruin of mechanisms and logs.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the island is abandoned, with Sentinels still active. No later developments were found.

42.content:
Land of Myriad Megaliths: The Land of Myriad Megaliths is a point of interest in the Sulfurous Veins area of Tequemecan Valley, Natlan. Its in-game viewpoint is titled Stone Chamber of Shifting Crystal Pillars.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 it remains an explorable location. No further information was found.

43.content:
Legendary Tonatiuh (also: Tonatiuh, Skyserpent Ship, Sky Serpent Ship, Legendary Skyserpent Ship): The Tonatiuh, also called the Skyserpent Ship, is a floating, dragon-built vessel high above the clouds over Ochkanatlan in Natlan. Legend made it Och-Kan's treasure ship, full of riches and containing a Jade of Return that could quell the Abyss, and adventurers chased it for generations. In fact it is a bleak, wind-scoured structure of islands and tangled lines, and the 'Jade' is a Golden Entreaty that Och-Kan hid there; Kukulkan invented the legend as a lure. As of 7.1 it is empty.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Tonatiuh is empty and quiet. The trap set there by the Sage of the Stolen Flame has been destroyed, and the Golden Entreaty has been recovered by the Traveler.

44.content:
Leisurely Puffer: A watersports shop in Toyac Springs, in the People of the Springs' area of Natlan, owned by the family of the surfer Mualani.

Status as of 7.1: Open as of 7.1.

45.content:
Malinalco Grotto: Malinalco Grotto is an underground cavern in Quahuacan Cliff, Natlan. It contains a mural depicting the legend of Kuntur and Rumi, and is reached by taking the right-hand tunnel at the entrance of the Tenebrous Papilla boss cave.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the grotto remains accessible. No later developments were found.

46.content:
Manse of Monetoo Murals: The Manse of Monetoo Murals is a point of interest on Teticpac Peak in Coatepec Mountain, Natlan. Its viewpoint is titled Where the Painted Realm Unfolds.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 it remains an explorable location. No further information was found.

47.content: Mare Jivari (also: Silent Sea of Ashes, Ashen Sea): The Mare Jivari ('Silent Sea of Ashes') was a region at the far west of Tenochtzitoc in Natlan, once a sea of fire and now described as an endless plain of ash where the wind does not blow. It earned its name in a great battle of the cataclysm, when Tenoch and Sanhaj Kompore destroyed the Bakunawa there. Barbatos later blew it off the timeline, so it is cut off from the world.

48.content:
Mother Flamegranate Tree: The Mother Flamegranate Tree is a great tree in Tequemecan Valley, Natlan, and the source of the Scions of the Canopy tribe's Flamegranates. Its roots, in a cave warmed by lava, grow the Mountain King Flamegranates.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the tree is ripe and still guarded by the Scions of the Canopy. No later changes were found.

49.content:
Muhuru's Gemporium: A gem shop in the Children of Echoes' settlement in Tequemecan Valley, Natlan, run by Cheven.

Status as of 7.1: Open as of 7.1.

50.content:
Natlan (also: Nation of War, Land of Saurians): Natlan is the nation of Pyro and of war in western Teyvat, beyond Sumeru's desert, a hot land of volcanoes, canyons, mesas and hot springs. Its people are the Natlanese, organised into six tribes, each bonded with one kind of Saurian, the evolved descendants of Natlan's ancient dragons. The Pyro Archon and God of War, currently Mavuika, is unlike other Archons: every Pyro Archon is a mortal human who won the throne through battle. For 500 years Natlan fought an unending war against the Abyss, until it was won in Archon Quest Chapter V.

Government: The Pyro Archon leads Natlan from the Speaker's Chamber at the Stadium of the Sacred Flame; each tribe has its own chief.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Natlan is at peace. The Abyss was purged from the Night Kingdom in 5.3 and the Night Warden Wars are over. Mavuika lives and still rules, because Capitano took her fated death upon himself. Natlanese may now leave the nation without harm, though they still need their chief's permission. Natlan no longer has its Pyro Gnosis.

51.content:
Natlantea (also: Natlantean civilization, Natlantean era): Natlantea was the civilisation that came before Natlan: an age when Pyro dragons ruled and humans lived in primitive tribes. Its lord was the Pyro Dragon Sovereign Xiuhcoatl, served by the Thirteen Sovereign Lords, and its greatest city was the Sacred City of Tollan. The era ended when Xbalanque united an army, defeated Xiuhcoatl and became the first Pyro Archon.

History: Natlantea ended in a war. Xbalanque rallied humans under one banner, laid siege to Tollan, killed ten of the Thirteen Sovereign Lords and the Three Princes, and fought Xiuhcoatl; the two fell together and Xbalanque emerged reborn as the first Pyro Archon. A treaty with Kukulkan followed, ending dragon rule.

key: Kingdom of the Lord of the Night
52.content:
Night Kingdom (also: Realm of the Wayob, Kingdom of the Lord of the Night, Land of Night): The Night Kingdom is a realm of souls deep beneath Natlan, described as "a liminal space between the body and mind, life and death". Yohualtecuhtin, the Lord of the Night, built it from the fragments of Natlan's ancient ley lines, which were shattered in the war of funerary flame. Since then it has worked as Natlan's ley lines. The tribes' ancestral spirits, the Wayob, live there, and so do the souls of Natlan's dead. Natlanese warriors draw their "Nightsoul" power from those souls. For five hundred years after the cataclysm the Abyss occupied the realm. The Traveler and Mavuika purged it in 5.3.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Night Kingdom is free of the Abyss and is being restored. The Lord of the Night is back inside it, maintaining Natlan's ley lines, and the Night Warden Wars are over.

53.content:
Nursery of Nightmares: The Nursery of Nightmares is a space resembling the Night Kingdom in Ochkanatlan, Natlan. It is where the Traveler finished the chase for the Dragon of the City of Flowing Ash in Moment of Awakening, where the dragon's corruption was purged and Och-Kan's soul was freed, and where Och-Kan's remains now lie.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Nursery is calm. Och-Kan's remains rest there; the dragon body and Cocouik's mind were reunited as Och-Kan, who died as the quest ended.

54.content:
Ochkanatlan (also: Cinder City): Ochkanatlan, the Cinder City, is a ruined island city in Natlan, north of Quahuacan Cliff. It was built thousands of years ago by followers of Xbalanque on the remains of an older dragon city, and was ruled by the tyrant Och-Kan, the Sacred Lord, in the era of the Grand Alliance. Today it is thick with Abyssal corruption, shrouded in mist, and forbidden to the tribes. Any human found inside is either a memory of the past or a trespasser.

Geography: A mist-covered island north of Quahuacan Cliff, with a castle-like structure, the Cradle of Fleeting Dreams, at its centre. Waterfalls and underground ruins lie below it. Above it, drifting over a sea of clouds, hangs the Tonatiuh.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Ochkanatlan is still a ruin and still officially forbidden, but the tainted dragon is gone.

55.content:
Old Core of Chu'ulel: The Old Core of Chu'ulel is a set of underground chambers beneath Ochkanatlan in Natlan. A giant dragon statue stands within, where Och-Kan trapped the Dragonlord Ix Uxul Tz'ib Bolon Ch'ule-L after seizing power in Ochkanatlan.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the chambers are open and the Dragonlord's soul has been freed. No later changes were found.

56.content:
Phlogiston Extraction Research Center (also: Extraction Research Center): A secret underground Fatui base inside Coatepec Mountain in Natlan. The Fatui extract Phlogiston there from captured Saurians, with machinery supplied by the Fontaine Research Institute.

Status as of 7.1: Active Fatui site as of 7.1; open to the player as a Point of Interest in Coatepec Mountain.

57.content:
Pseudostar Pedestal: A subarea in the Dragons' Residence of the Ancient Sacred Mountain (the Sacred City of Tollan) in Natlan, next to a teleport waypoint.

Status as of 7.1: Accessible as of 7.1, the same as the rest of the Ancient Sacred Mountain.

58.content: Pyro Archon Temple: The Pyro Archon Temple is a hidden temple under the Easybreeze Holiday Resort area of Natlan, first entered in the quest The Last Survivor of Tenochtzitoc (5.8). Citlali guesses it was built about five hundred years ago by Pyro Archons to hold the Bakunawa. Its central stone structure opens onto the Night Kingdom and the Mare Jivari.

59.content:
Quahuacan Cliff: Quahuacan Cliff is the cliff-top home of the Flower-Feather Clan (Tlalocan), the Natlan tribe that rides Qucusaurs, the flying saurians. The clan's riders once patrolled all of Natlan and still watch the ruins of Ochkanatlan. Since 5.8 the cliff also serves as the landing for people leaving Nod-Krai. The name may echo the Nahuatl Cuauhhuacan, a place name built from the words for tree and eagle.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the clan is at peace, and the cliff doubles as a haven for Nod-Krai refugees and merchants.

60.content:
Realm of the Night Kingdom: The "Realm of the Night Kingdom" is a quest domain in Natlan's Basin of Unnumbered Flames, entered during the Archon Quest "Into Eternal Night". The domain's own description calls it the realm of the dead, where the "River of Concepts" flows, and says Kachina is trapped here, struggling desperately and needing rescue before it is too late.

Status as of 7.1: A quest-only domain; no standing gameplay use after the quest per the wiki's "temporary" navbox. The Night Kingdom itself persists in Natlan lore as of 7.1.

key: Remnants of the Secret Source excavation site
61.content: Remnants of Tetenanco (also: Remnants of the Secret Source excavation site): The Remnants of Tetenanco are ancient ruins left by the dragons in Atocpan, Natlan. They are thought to be a satellite city destroyed in the war between the dragons and Xbalanque, the first Pyro Archon. Locals now call them the Remnants of the Secret Source excavation site.

62.content:
Remnants of the Secret Source: Remnants of the Secret Source is the ruined former home of ancient dragonkind in Natlan's Basin of Unnumbered Flames, and the only path to the Night Kingdom. Influenced by the Abyss, it hides many unforeseen dangers. It is a quest domain entered during the Archon Quest "Echoes of Life".

Status as of 7.1: A quest domain; the Night Kingdom beyond it is the destination, and as of 7.1 nothing further is added to the domain.

63.content:
Ruined Armament Workshop: A ruined facility in the Dragons' Residence of the Ancient Sacred Mountain, Natlan. It once made and stored weapons, and the ancient dragons may also have used it for human experimentation.

Status as of 7.1: Ruined and accessible as of 7.1.

key: Ruins of the Sage of the Stolen Flame
64.comment: Ruins of the Sage of the Stolen Flame
64.content: Ruins of the Sage of the Stolen Flame: The Ruins of the Sage of the Stolen Flame are an instance in Tequemecan Valley, Natlan, unlocked during the quest Revelations from the Past. After the quest, one reaches them from the Hall of Parting Vows by descending glowing stairs to Catastrophe's Edge and touching an inscription.

65.content:
Sacrificial Altar of Enigmatic Land: The Sacrificial Altar of Enigmatic Land is a point of interest in the Tezcatepetonco Range of Natlan, within the area of the Masters of the Night-Wind. Its viewpoint is called Ceremonial Site Lost in Night's Dim Light.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 it is an accessible location with named residents. No later changes were found.

66.content:
Sanctum of Rainbow Spirits: The Sanctum of Rainbow Spirits is an empty trial ground in Ameyalco Waters, Toyac Springs, Natlan. Tradition says the first sage to learn phlogiston created a place of great purity here, where warriors were taught to wield prismatic flames and flowing light. The sanctum is now abandoned and occupied by scoundrels.

Status as of 7.1: Permanently accessible in Natlan as of 7.1; no plot events are tied to it.

67.content: Scorchwind Trial Grounds (also: Pakpaka Flying School): The Scorchwind Trial Grounds is a training ground in the Tezcatepetonco Range of Natlan, south of the "Masters of the Night-Wind" tribe. It is the base of the Pakpaka Flying School, which teaches flying with Qucusaurs.

68.content:
Sea of Shifting Sentience: A subarea of the Ancient Sacred Mountain in Natlan with large pools of Liquid Phlogiston. The ancient dragons once submerged themselves in them to take in the knowledge and wisdom stored in the primal flame.

Status as of 7.1: Accessible as of 7.1.

69.content: Seven-Colored Statue: The Seven-Colored Statue is a large statue in the Easybreeze Market of Natlan's Easybreeze Holiday Resort. It resembles an octopus spouting seven bubbles.

70.content:
Seven-Hued Ruins: The Seven-Hued Ruins are the underground remains of the Battle of Seven Colors in Natlan's Tezcatepetonco Range. Citlali, following directions from Etchemin, finds the entrance to the ruined battlefield, and the Traveller goes in with her. The domain's text notes that the secrets of the battle turned out to be buried deep beneath the ground.

Status as of 7.1: A quest-only domain as of 7.1; its walkthrough on the wiki is incomplete.

71.content:
Skyfire Circlet (also: Nahuatzin's Springboard): The Skyfire Circlet is a ring of islands floating over the mouth of the Great Volcano of Tollan in Natlan, suspended by the power of Phlogiston. It contains the only entrance to the Ancient Sacred Mountain, which is why it is also called Nahuatzin's Springboard.

Status as of 7.1: Open as of 7.1; no appearance in 6.x or 7.0-7.1 content was found.

72.content:
Speaker's Chamber (also: Speakers' Chamber): The Speaker's Chamber is a watchtower-like building in a corner of the Stadium of the Sacred Flame. The Pyro Archon presides over it, and it coordinates the Stadium's affairs and the six major tribes.

Status as of 7.1: Active as the Stadium's council hall as of 7.1.

73.content: Spiritwall Cave: Spiritwall Cave is a point of interest in Toyac Springs, Natlan. It is a closed-off cave where someone left a half-written, half-drawn note describing years spent making wall paintings.

74.content:
Stadium of the Sacred Flame (also: Sacred Flame Arena): The Stadium of the Sacred Flame is the heart of Natlan, a great arena in the Basin of Unnumbered Flames that serves as the nation's main city and the common ground of its six tribes. Above the arena burns the Sacred Flame, the ever-burning fire that holds back the Abyss and links the living world to the Night Kingdom. Here Natlan held the Pilgrimage of the Return of the Sacred Flame, its great combat tournament, and the Ode of Resurrection that brought fallen heroes back to life; here too stands the Speaker's Chamber, where the Pyro Archon Mavuika governs. Since the Abyss was defeated (5.3) the Stadium is a place of peace and sport.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Natlan is at peace. The Night Warden Wars are over, so the Ode of Resurrection is no longer held and Ancient Name bearers no longer have to compete. Mavuika has turned the Pilgrimage into a purely athletic competition, which opens the possibility of outsiders taking part.

key: Stadium of the Sacred Flame: Chuwen Fair
75.comment: Stadium of the Sacred Flame: Chuwen Fair
75.content:
Stadium of the Sacred Flame: Chuwen Fair (also: Chuwen Fair): The fair along the northern side of the Stadium of the Sacred Flame in the Basin of Unnumbered Flames, Natlan, on the Fair and Temple map level.

Status as of 7.1: Open and populated as of 7.1.

key: Stadium of the Sacred Flame: Temple of Pax
76.comment: Stadium of the Sacred Flame: Temple of Pax
76.content:
Stadium of the Sacred Flame: Temple of Pax (also: Temple of Pax): A section of the Stadium of the Sacred Flame along its southern side, in the Basin of Unnumbered Flames. It has an outer concourse and an inner fair-and-temple area, and seems to handle scholarship on ancient dragon relics.

Status as of 7.1: Open and populated as of 7.1.

key: Stadium of the Sacred Flame: Warrior's Rest Area
77.comment: Stadium of the Sacred Flame: Warrior's Rest Area
77.content:
Stadium of the Sacred Flame: Warrior's Rest Area (also: Warrior's Rest Area): A rest area within the Stadium of the Sacred Flame, in the Basin of Unnumbered Flames, Natlan, serving the stadium's fighters and visitors.

Status as of 7.1: Open and populated as of 7.1.

78.content:
Stage Tepetl: A grand stage in the Children of Echoes' settlement in Tequemecan Valley, Natlan, where the tribe hosts dance battles every day and night.

Status as of 7.1: In use for dance battles as of 7.1.

79.content:
Stone Stele Records (also: Reflection: The Deep, Transient Void): Stone Stele Records is a Trounce (weekly boss) domain in Natlan's Tezcatepetonco Range. It represents a huge stone tablet raised in Natlan, carved with the image of a new hero, and lets players relive the battle against the Lord of Eroded Primal Fire. It is unlocked during the Archon Quest "When All Becomes a Monument".

Status as of 7.1: Permanently available as of 7.1 as a replay of the final battle of the Natlan Archon Quest.

80.content: Sulfurous Veins (also: Shadow Pins): Sulfurous Veins is a subarea of Tequemecan Valley in Natlan. It is a rugged, sulfur-bright stretch of rock known for enormous nails of solid Phlogiston, called "Shadow Pins".

81.content:
Summoning Hall: The entrance hall of the Sacred City of Tollan in the Ancient Sacred Mountain, Natlan, connected to the volcano's mouth at the Skyfire Circlet.

Status as of 7.1: Accessible as of 7.1.

82.content: Tablet of Tona: The Tablet of Tona is a stone wheel enshrined in the Temple of Pax, inside the Stadium of the Sacred Flame in Natlan. It stands as a symbol of unity in Natlan between humans, Saurians, the Sacred Flame and the Pyro Archon.

83.content: Tecoloapan Bay (also: Tecoloapan Beach, Lost Ceremonial Site): Tecoloapan Bay is an island west of Tezcatepetonco Range in Natlan. It starts covered in thick fog, hidden from the map and labelled "???" until the world quest The Mystery of Tecoloapan Beach is completed.

key: Temple of Cascading Colors: Ch'upikaq Tajin
84.comment: Temple of Cascading Colors: Ch'upikaq Tajin
84.content:
Temple of Cascading Colors: Ch'upikaq Tajin (also: Ch'upikaq Tajin, Temple of Cascading Colors): The Temple of Cascading Colors: Ch'upikaq Tajin is a ruined site at Quahuacan Cliff in Natlan, entered in the Archon Quest "Searing" while following Ineffa. The domain text says Source Servants once offered flowers and candles here to the Eighth (Ix Ajkotz'i'j Iq'ismal Waxak), but the flowers have withered and the candlelight has died; only winds whisper old stories.

Status as of 7.1: A quest-only domain as of 7.1. The temple stays a ruin of withered offerings.

85.content: Tepeacac Rise (also: Genesis of the Mountains): Tepeacac Rise is a stretch of slopes in the northwest of Coatepec Mountain in Natlan. The lower ground is unusually good for plant growth, so Saurians often rest there; Natlan also calls the slopes the "Genesis of the Mountains".

86.content:
Tequemecan Valley: Tequemecan Valley is the mining country of eastern Natlan and the home of the Children of Echoes (Nanatzcayan), the tribe of miners, gem appraisers and craftspeople who live in a gorge with their burrowing Tepetlisaur companions. Clanging hammers and tapping gem-hunters echo through the canyon, and dance battles are held daily. Beneath the valley the Shadow Pins keep the Abyss sealed, and the ruins of an ancient oath lie below its hills.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the valley is quiet; the Shadow Pins hold, and the tribe's music and mining carry on.

87.content: Tete Isle (also: Tete Island): Tete Isle is a subarea of Easybreeze Holiday Resort, the summer resort island off Natlan's far west. It is known for a lively atmosphere and its specialty drink, Aphimead, and becomes accessible at step 5 of the story quest The World Is Your Canvas! (Sunspray Summer Resort, Part II).

88.content: Teticpac Peak: Teticpac Peak is a plateau with a small lake at the highest point of Coatepec Mountain in Natlan. It contains the Manse of Monetoo Murals.

89.content:
Tezcatepetonco Range: The Tezcatepetonco Range is the highland home of the Masters of the Night-Wind (Mictlan), Natlan's shamans and mystics, who speak with the Wayob, watch over the ley lines and Phlogiston, read futures and heal. The tribe is reclusive and eccentric and has the deepest bond with the Night Kingdom of any Natlan tribe. A fog-covered island, Tecoloapan Bay, lies off the range. In Nahuatl, Tezcatepetonco means 'mirror on the hill'.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the tribe is at peace, and Tecoloapan Bay is free of fog and seals.

90.content:
The Mysterious Island's Truth: The Mysterious Island's Truth is a quest domain in Ameyalco Waters, Toyac Springs, Natlan: an underground lava cave the party enters through a giant whirlpool during Mualani's story quest of the same name. The name is the wiki's unofficial label.

Status as of 7.1: A quest-only domain as of 7.1; the wiki entry is a stub.

91.content:
The Salutary Furnace: A blacksmith's stall in the Stadium of the Sacred Flame, owned by Alom, built around a giant furnace at one side of the Temple of Pax.

Status as of 7.1: Open as of 7.1.

92.content:
The Upper Sanctum (also: Upper Sanctum, Hanan Pacha): The Upper Sanctum, also called Hanan Pacha, is a ring of floating islands above the lake at Ameyalco Waters in Toyac Springs, Natlan. Legend says the Sage of the Stolen Flame and his companion Chaac raised it into the sky, and that people who passed his trials were taught to use phlogiston there and formed the first human tribe. The islands are said to be held together by Phlogiston. A trial ends at a hidden hot spring in the centre.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Upper Sanctum remains a broken ring of islands whose trials and hot spring still function. Chikya soaks in the spring and returns to her scrolls.

93.content: Throne of the Primal Fire: The Throne of the Primal Fire is a site in Ochkanatlan where the throne of the first Pyro Archon, Xbalanque, once stood. The map text says he borrowed the Ruler of Death's power here to establish Natlan's rules.

94.content: Tlazolli's Forge (also: Tlazolli's Workshop): Tlazolli's Forge is the workshop of the Ancient Name forger Tlazolli in Tequemecan Valley, Natlan. It was announced as abandoned and sealed after she stepped down from her tribal position, but in the quest Wailing Cacophony (5.1) it proves to be where she tries to turn an orphaned girl into her dead daughter Nechca.

95.content:
Tlazolli's Home (also: Tlazolli's house, Tlazolli's workshop): Tlazolli's Home is the dwelling and workshop of Tlazolli, an Ancient Name forger of the Children of Echoes, on the outskirts of the tribe's settlement in Tequemecan Valley, Natlan. Its interior can be entered only during the quest Melodious Chant. It is where Nechca's birthday party is held and where a mother's grief turned into a harmful deception.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the home is closed off by the tribe after Tlazolli's crimes; she is in custody and Nepecha stays with Xilonen.

96.content:
Toyac Springs: Toyac Springs is the hot-spring coast of Natlan and the home of the People of the Springs (Meztli), a tribe of guides, cartographers, musicians and spa-keepers who live with their water-loving Koholasaurs. Official text calls it the most popular tribe region with outside visitors. Its name resembles the Nahuatl atoyac, 'on the river'.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the tribe is at peace and Toyac Springs is the most popular holiday stop in Natlan.

97.content:
Underground Lava River (also: Lava River, Underground Lava River: Upper Level, Underground Lava River: Lower Level): The Underground Lava River is a cavern under Ameyalco Waters in Toyac Springs, Natlan, filled with liquid Phlogiston and subject to periodic eruptions. It is the only known source of Vulcanite, a rare golden crystal formed when liquid phlogiston cools quickly; this glow is what the People of the Springs' legend of the 'Mysterious Island' points toward. Koholasaurs live here, and an old trial door in its ruins opens a Spiritway to the Upper Sanctum.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the cavern remains hot and active, with Koholasaurs living in it. Vulcanite still cannot be brought back, and the Spiritway trial is solved.

98.content: Varesa's Orchard: Varesa's Orchard is a family orchard just outside the "Collective of Plenty" tribe's settlement in Atocpan, Natlan. It belongs to Varesa and is guarded by her Tatankasaur companion, Vanana.

99.content: Villa Guiztli (also: The Town in the Rock): Villa Guiztli is an underground town beneath Guiztli Ridge, a small rocky island in Easybreeze Holiday Resort. It is inhabited by cardboard cutouts and Nochtlins, and offers an immersive experience in which visitors play heroes defending the town from the villain "El Capoctus Joquiratto".

100.content:
Vision Serpent's Sanctum (also: Vision Serpent Sanctum): The Vision Serpent's Sanctum is a site in Ochkanatlan listed beneath the Cradle of Fleeting Dreams. It has a mural and a note written by the Holy Sovereign.

Status as of 7.1: Ruined and open for exploration as of 7.1.

101.content:
Vucub Caquix Tower (also: Fire Parrot Tower): The Vucub Caquix Tower stands in the middle of Ashflow Street in Ochkanatlan. Its lower level, reached by elevator, holds notes from different eras about an expedition into the city and the calamity that ended the old alliance.

Status as of 7.1: Ruined and silent as of 7.1; open for exploration.

102.content: Wavey Bay: Wavey Bay is the seaside subarea of Easybreeze Holiday Resort in Natlan, known for sandy beaches, pristine waters and many aquatic attractions.

103.content:
Weary Inn (also: Inn of Lassitude): The Weary Inn is a restaurant and hotel in one, on the outskirts of the Chuwen Fair in the Stadium of the Sacred Flame (Warrior's Rest Area), Natlan. It offers free lodging and food to warriors taking part in the Pilgrimage of the Return of the Sacred Flame.

Status as of 7.1: Open as of 7.1 under Chanca.

104.content: Well of Seven Flames: The Well of Seven Flames is a point of interest on Ashflow Street in Ochkanatlan, Natlan. Canon read gives no description of it beyond its name and place on the map.

105.content: Xalac Vale (also: Xalac Valley): Xalac Vale is a river valley in Natlan. It extends from the Stadium of the Sacred Flame to the Flower-Feather Clan's lands, and on its north side it runs past the Masters of the Night-Wind. It is a travel corridor between the tribes rather than a settlement, and canon says little more about it.

106.content:
Xocolatl Beverages: Xocolatl Beverages is a juice bar in the Stadium of the Sacred Flame in Natlan, run by Yantasar of the Masters of the Night-Wind. It specialises in unconventional drinks made from fresh fruit and spices, which locals enjoy.

Status as of 7.1: Open as of 7.1; nothing about it has changed in canon.

107.content:
Yumemizuki's Cozy Corner (also: Cozy Corner): Yumemizuki's Cozy Corner is a small store in the People of the Springs' area of Toyac Springs, Natlan, that offers psychotherapy through dream-eating yumekui-baku. It is presumably owned by Yumemizuki Mizuki, the Inazuman clinical psychologist and Aisa Bathhouse shareholder, and is currently staffed by a baku named Mint Daifuku.

Status as of 7.1: Open as of 7.1, minded by Mint Daifuku. The owner is not present.

108.content:
Zakan's Street Bites (also: Zakan's Food Stall): Zakan's Street Bites is a food stall near the Weary Inn's entrance in the Stadium of the Sacred Flame, Natlan. Run by Chanca, it is described as Natlan's main restaurant and sells hearty meals, ingredients and recipes.

Status as of 7.1: Open as of 7.1 under Chanca.
